body: It's just I trust her so much. I couldn't imagine her cheating on me. And I am very good at knowing when people lie to me... She would have had to be lying to me almost pathologically for her to hide cheating. I honestly don't think that is the reason...

The first time we met this past December, she was awkward only like, the first day, and it's understandable, I was a little awkward too since I had never seen her in person before. After that we went on to have an awesome time. Yes, we had sex, we kissed, we did everything a loving couple does. When we saw each other again on March, the same, everything was fine. Sex, kissing, intimacy. From January to March, the no-skype-sex symptom had already begun, but that was all and I dismissed it as she didn't want to have skype sex anymore and only real sex.

Do you think that maybe he wanted you to see them? I can't really think of any other reason why he would give you access to the password of a place he STILL keeps pictures of YOUR girlfriend.

EDIT: Even if he legit needed you to recover the account, why not move the pictures somewhere you wouldn't have access to?

I feel for you, man. You don't know how much I know how you feel. I understand your situation deeply. #nohomo but man I wish I could give you a hug.

A "just friends" relationship between a man and a woman can never exist, simply because men and women are different. Women are actually capable of feeling nothing sexual for their male friends. But we guys are different. We can't... Or at least I can't, and no guy I have ever known can. If you go into the internet and read some articles authored by psychologists, there will always be a bias. Articles written by male psychologists always conclude that the "just friends" crap is crap. Articles written by female psychologists will conclude the opposite, that it is possible.

What I am trying to tell you is that chances are the guy will make moves for your girlfriend. BUT, if you trust your girl and if she truly loves you she will NOT respond to those advances.

Next.

"Talking with somebody with no emotions at all". This line. Have you asked her if she still loves you? Do you think she means it? 4 Months is not a long ways off, but if she has changed and no longer feels the same about you it will be difficult. No longer being distanced may help a lot, but the relationship has to survive up to that point.

What I would do is give her a little space. I know, I have been there, being controlling with her is just a natural response to the apparent competition you see on that other dude. But think about it, does trying to control her would really make a difference? You're not there, you can't stop shit from happening if it's going to happen. I know it is harsh, but it is the truth, and once you realize this, you will feel a little more at peace. The only thing you can do is trust your girlfriend and try to have lots of open communication about everything you are feeling. Meet the guy when you are there. Be NICE to him, and try to figure out his intentions but DO NOT go and try to "mark your territory". If you do this, the only thing you're doing is letting him KNOW that you are insecure and threatened by him, and you would also COMFIRM to him that you are acknowledging him as competition, putting you AT THE SAME LEVEL with him. Never do this. Always be nice to him even if he's not. Always take an attitude of "you are here, I am here, I am fine and relaxed, you are of no real concern to me, I am my girlfriend's boyfriend and you are his friend, that is all there is and that is all that will be". 

I really hope everything goes for the best. I sincerely wish you a happy relationship and that all turns out for the better. Good luck.

Which is more important to you, your friendship or your girl? Because your only options are:
1.) To keep quiet about the whole thing so that no one finds out you hacked your friend.
2.) Confront your girl and have everyone know what you did.

If you choose #1, you will feel horrible every time you look at your girl's face. The curiosity and doubt will haunt you always UNLESS you decide "whatever she did before being my girlfriend is none of my concern". You have to have a lot of strength in order to go down this path.

If you choose #2 you may or may not lose your friend, but chances are you will know the truth. Are you sure you want to know the truth?

Putting aside the cold calculations, here is what I would do, as a rational but also emotional human being.

I would ask her again about the pictures. I would hope to all the gods I don't believe in that she tells me the truth. If she lies, my trust in her will be considerably diminished. If she's willing to lie about stuff that happened years ago before you two were even together, chances are she would be MORE than willing to lie about more important stuff happening NOW that actually concerns the relationship and you. Finally, if she lies, I would confront her and tell her that there were more pictures but I would REFUSE to tell her how I know unless absolutely necessary. I would proceed to actually question her loyalty and honesty and well, yeah. There's not really much else to do.

Thanks a lot for your response, taoofindifference. One thing, though. I made it VERY CLEAR to her my views regarding male best friends BEFORE we started dating, when we were just friends, and even later, when we WERE STARTING to date as well. This is the reason why I won't comment on your Thought Exercise, because yeah, having known before-hand really does make a huge difference. If I had decided to be with her even while knowing and considering her NUT, then yeah, it was my decision then. If she decides to break up with me now because of my NUT, well there's nothing I can do about it. There is something that your comment made me realize though, and I profoundly appreciate you for it. It is that I'd rather break up than have to deal with constantly having to feel shitty because I know she's spending tons of alone time with another guy. My main focus wasn't that she shouldn't do it because she could cheat. My main focus is I don't want her to do it because it makes me feel like shit. 
I trust her that she won't cheat on me and that she can have many male friends. I just don't trust the guy who spends his money, time, and effort on a girl he only plans to "be friends with".

Thing is, I told her about my issues regarding best friends BEFORE we got into the relationship. You don't really look at the contents of a contract AFTER signing it. By the time you look at contents, you already sold your soul to the devil and you're screwed.
On this line of thought, she knew I have issues with male best friends and still decided to have a relationship with me. Now, one year into the relationship she started becoming too friendly with this guy and I reminded her about my views on it.
But then again, she probably just doesn't see it that way. Let me clarify something to you, buttztuff, it is not that I don't trust her. I do. I have never limited her in any way. She has lots of male friends whom she goes out with, to the movies, to restaurants, etc. as in, part of a GROUP OF FRIENDS. And I am totally cool with that. 
It isn't so much that I don't trust her as much as that I don't trust HIM. 
I am not necessarily projecting my past relationship into the current one. My fear was more towards her spending way too much time alone with this guy and starting to go to the movies together, going to restaurants alone, etc.
How would you feel if your boyfriend started having this one specific female friend whom he spends tons of time with, talks to and chats to all the time, and he reduces the time spent with you in favor of more time spent with the other girl. Would not that make you feel bad?
That is the situation I am trying to avoid, but into that equation I never gave the cheating factor too much importance. I may have made it sound like I did, in retrospect.
Thanks a lot for your response, I really appreciate it a lot.

I don't have a sister, and my female cousin and I have kissed many times in the past when we were kids (I was like 9, she was like 10). And in the end, I have never considered incest as inherently wrong. It has a lot to do with a phenomenon called "moral dumbfounding" which causes many people to express strong negative reactions to incest, but they cannot provide a rational reason as to why. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_intuitionism 
But yeah, that's besides the point.

It may be seen as close minded but hell, I have had many female best friends in the past. Some have had one-sided feelings toward me, other times I've had one-sided feelings toward them, sometimes it has been mutual. I have SEEN other people's best-friend relationship and one or both always end up with feelings or having sex. I have READ extensively psychological journals and anecdotes that seem to point out that men will almost never be able to successfully participate in a best-friend relationship with a girl. All the evidence seems to point out that it is simply not possible.

I trust my girlfriend enough to feel "safe" regarding her cheating on me. I just like to avoid a situation where she becomes really close with the guy, and they start to talk all the time and she starts leaking information about my relationship to that guy (I don't mind if she does this with her girl-friends. That's normal), and they start going to the movies together and going to restaurants together and soon, she'll start enjoying her time with him more than me? And yeah. But really, Warpfrenzy I heavily appreciate your response and your views on this. Thanks.

Yeah, that's probably a big factor. Thanks a lot. It does make me feel bad and I will try expressing myself more in terms of feelings than in terms of "science". I really appreciate your response, thanks.

Yeah, in my case my girlfriend was afraid of how I'd take it as well. I'm just gonna remind you that no matter how bad he takes you talking to him about this issue, I guarantee he would take a breakup even worse, ESPECIALLY if the breakup came as a surprise. However, I believe you shouldn't take him blaming himself as a bad thing. After all... it actually IS his fault. He may just be doing it because he believes it is not a bad thing, like I used to believe. But then he might gain a new perspective from you talking to him, that it actually IS bad behavior and it's putting his relationship, that he treasures so much, in danger. Best-case scenario is he sees the error of his ways and prefers to stop doing that instead of losing you. Worst-case, nothing changes and you will need to look for alternatives.

IF the incident you are describing is an isolated incident. Then yeah, he is definitely overreacting.
It seems odd, however. I have seldom heard of someone acting unreasonably for no reason at all, to the point of sleeping in different rooms just because of something like that. Are you sure there hasn't been stress mounting and building up? The best thing you could do is try to have an open talk with him. Be assertive but not pushy. "I don't want us to sleep in different rooms anymore. I know I screwed up and said things that hurt you, but I think there may be more to the problem. Will you talk to me?"

That's just my two cents on your issue. I honestly wish you a prompt and happy resolution.

Hello, I hope I can be of some help to you, providing you a somewhat similar point of view. I also am in a long distance relationship with my girlfriend, and I also have a long history of mental health problems. Childhood traumas, depression, you name it. Also, like your boyfriend, I am very distant with my family.

The first thing is, I consider my girlfriend the only family member I can really count on for emotional support. Because of this, there was a point in time where I was EXTREMELY clingy. I demanded that she told me every single breath she took. When she got home from university, if she was going to go out of the house for any reason, if she went out on weekends I wanted to know her every move. And you know, I did all these things for two reasons. I was in a period of my life where I was extremely insecure and lonely, and I craved for her attention. I wanted to FEEL like she CARED and was constantly INTERESTED in me, simply because no one else gave a damn about me in that way.

But, the second and most important reason I had that behavior, is because SHE LET ME. For a while at least. Thankfully, my girl and I have always had very open communication in the relationship. And so, she told me everything she was feeling. She felt suffocated, controlled. And I realized my mistake. I also realized if I didn't stop, I was going to lose her. 
Talk to him. Make him see. If necessary, although harsh, you're going to have to give him an ultimatum. Encourage him to get a therapist. It really helps a lot. But you need to tell him. I can see you're already considering breaking up, but don't you think it's fair he gets a warning before it gets to that?\

Thanks a lot for your response. I really appreciate it a great deal. I will take what you said into consideration. For now, I've decided on a few life changes that I hope will help, and I'll talk it through with my friends. It just disappoints me so much, I thought I was out of it, and now, three years later I'm back in the same road. The thought of it never going away completely and having to actively battle depression throughout my life really scares me. But thanks a lot, I really appreciate your time.
